title: Brazil votes as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro lead the polls
summary:
People in Brazil began voting on 4 October 2026. Twelve candidates want to be president. Current president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro lead opinion polls—surveys asking people whom they support.

Lula belongs to the left-wing Workers’ Party. Flávio is a right-wing politician and former president Jair Bolsonaro’s son. Left-wing and right-wing mean different ideas about running a country.

Four years ago, Lula beat Jair Bolsonaro by a small amount. Jair is not running now. He is under house arrest after being found guilty of planning to overturn the election result. He cannot post on social media or make public statements. The source says he supports his son’s campaign.

Only Lula and Flávio have at least 10% support in polls. Surveys suggest a second vote, called a run-off, is very likely. But many voters had not decided shortly before election day. Someone could still win in the first round.

Almost 160 million Brazilians can vote. People can start voting at 16. Those aged 18 to 70 who can read and write must vote or face a fine. Polls usually ask only thousands of people, so results may be very different.

Lula is 80 and has been president three times. During his first two terms, from 2003 to 2010, many praised his Bolsa Família cash-support programme for helping millions leave poverty. His later convictions for corruption and money laundering were cancelled in 2021. He has always denied those crimes.

Some environmentalists have criticised recent actions. Lula says oil money can help pay for cleaner energy. He says he still plans to end fossil-fuel use eventually. His government points to satellite information suggesting Amazon forest loss in the first half of 2026 reached its lowest level in ten years.
